mode: one bounded fresh-context final-artifact recheck; read-only source review

scope.boundary: All entrypoints and workflow-owned operative procedural references/helpers were read. Large Linux, document-format, GEO and vehicle factual packs have explicitly bounded coverage below. This is not a full factual recertification.
excluded_inputs: labeled trigger projections and canonical trigger corpora
scope.execution_boundary: No research workflow, model/provider invocation, SSH, live personal store, daemon/service, index write or source repair was performed. Disposable helper checks used temporary directories and disabled Python bytecode writes.
scope.independence: The reviewer used only final source artifacts, the allowlisted stripped input and the frozen procedure. The parent received findings after independent corroboration.

findings.title: Two raw captures in one second use the same exclusive filename
findings.quote: stamp = now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d-%H%M%S"); path = os.path.join(RAW_DIR, f"{stamp}.md"); with open(path, "xb") as f:
findings.behavior: The filename has only second precision and the exclusive create has no collision retry. A second capture during that second raises FileExistsError before saving its payload. The first capture remains intact.

corroboration.kind: EXECUTED disposable helper check plus second source read
corroboration.fixture: Temporary BRAINDUMP_DIR; now() fixed at 2026-11-11 12:00:00; call save_raw twice with distinct nonempty strings.
corroboration.observed: FileExistsError on the second call; one raw file after two attempts.

findings.severity_basis: Canonical Medium: reduces capture robustness without overwriting the existing immutable capture. Pass F covers an unhandled valid-input edge case.
findings.recommendation: Allocate a collision-safe unique raw filename while retaining exclusive creation and byte preservation; add an isolated two-captures-at-one-timestamp regression.
findings.scope: Source/helper defect; no claim about installed runtime state.

findings.title: The task parser silently reclassifies text after a middle-dot separator as metadata
findings.behavior: render_todo stores user text and metadata using an unescaped ' · ' separator. parse_todo splits at its first occurrence, so a valid task containing that separator loses part of its actionable text in list/export/bridge output.

corroboration.kind: EXECUTED disposable helper roundtrip plus second source read
corroboration.fixture: new_item('Review auth · staging checklist', meta='added 2026-11-11'); render_todo to a temporary Markdown file; parse_todo of that file.

findings.severity_basis: Canonical High (wrong output folded into High for skills): an ordinary accepted task does not round-trip with its meaning intact, contrary to the entrypoint's keep-the-user's-meaning rule. The defect is deterministic.
findings.recommendation: Use an unambiguous/escaped representation for user text and metadata, preserving existing item ids and legacy records; verify render/parse/export roundtrips for text containing the separator.
findings.scope: Source/helper defect; no SSH, extension or live-store execution was used.

helper_checks.level: EXECUTED disposable helper checks, separate from the 33 behavior predictions
helper_checks.temporary_store_cleanup: TemporaryDirectory cleanup completed in the same command; no test artifacts were written to target skill sources.

external_limits: Installed-copy parity, loaded entrypoint identity and live invocation are not tested. A source review or matching entrypoint hash cannot establish installed activation.

Live hub_route, semantic/keyword indexes, current hub manifests, registry, wrapper aliases and complete ecosystem peer resolution were not accessed. No missing installation/index dependency is counted as a source defect.
Office provider assets/recalculation engines were read as conditional dependencies only; no document/spreadsheet provider was executed.
Research adapters, shared runtimes, source libraries, external tree APIs and final research projections were not executed or certified.

Current legal rules, auction fees, hardware/runtime claims, library versions and AI-engine statistics were not browsed or recertified. The source's current-primary-evidence requirements remain operative.

Eval-file existence was checked without reading its labeled contents. Trigger accuracy thresholds cannot be calculated from unlabeled queries, and predicted functional compliance is not observed output.
Source hashes were stable between the two hash passes and match all supplied entrypoint bindings. Files only hashed or routed are not represented as fully read.
